nodes.characterization_summary: PtCu₂/CuO coating surface shows morphology with grooves and small protrusions; PtCu₂ shows grooves; CuO shows small protrusions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscope (SEM) analysis revealed that the surface of the PtCu₂/CuO coating exhibits a morphology characterized by a mixture of grooves and small protrusions. In contrast, the surfaces of the CuO and PtCu₂ coatings are dominated by small protrusions and grooves, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows clear contrast between bright Pt/Cu-enriched phase and dark Cu/O-enriched phase in PtCu₂/CuO coating with transition layer to Ti substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field transmission electron microscope (HAADF-STEM) image reveals a clear contrast between bright and dark phases within the coating.

nodes.characterization_summary: CuO region: crystal planes 2.52 Å (-111) and 2.53 Å (002); PtCu₂ region: 2.21 Å (111) and 1.95 Å (200) of FCC phase; interface shows PtCu₂(111)||CuO(002) orientation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the PtCu₂ metal phase, as shown in Figure 2e, the spacings between the adjacent lattice fringes are measured to be 2.21 and 1.95Å, corresponding to the (111) and (200) crystal planes of face-centered-cubic (FCC) metal phase, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms Pt:Cu atomic ratio close to 1:2 and Cu:O ratio close to 1:1; element distribution shows Pt/Cu enrichment in bright phase and Cu/O in dark phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The analysis of EDS line-scan data reveals that the atomic ratio of Pt and Cu is close to 1:2, while the atomic ratio of Cu and O is close to 1:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: GPA strain distribution at heterojunction interface shows tensile stress in FCC PtCu₂ phase and compressive stress in CuO phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the strain distribution image at the heterojunction interface based on the geometric phase analysis (GPA) method presents obvious strain fluctuations.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms coexistence of CuO monoclinic and FCC PtCu₂ metal phases; diffraction peaks for PtCu₂ between elemental Pt and Cu positions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns also confirm the coexistence of the CuO and FCC metal phases in the PtCu₂/CuO coating.

nodes.characterization_summary: In PtCu₂/CuO, Cu²⁺ increases to 57.1% (from 16.0% in PtCu₂), Pt²⁺ to 32.3% (from 12.4%); positive shift of Pt⁰ BE indicates electron transfer from PtCu₂ to CuO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the XPS peak area ratio, the proportions of Pt²⁺ and Cu²⁺ increase, respectively, from 12.4% to 32.3% and from 16.0% to 57.1% after heterostructure formation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge XANES shows increased white line intensity for PtCu₂/CuO vs Pt foil indicating higher Pt oxidation state; Cu K-edge shows metallic Cu in PtCu₂ and oxidized Cu in PtCu₂/CuO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the introduction of CuO, the WL intensity for PtCu₂/CuO is higher than that for Pt foil, but much lower than that for PtO₂, indicating that electrons will transfer from PtCu₂ to CuO.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows Pt-O, Cu-O, Pt-O-Cu and Cu-O-Cu bonds in PtCu₂/CuO along with metallic Pt-Pt/Cu and Cu-Pt/Cu bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the corresponding extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra for the Pt L₃-edge and Cu K-edge, PtCu₂/CuO not only exhibits Pt-Pt/Cu and Cu-Pt/Cu bonds belonging to the metallic state, but also Pt-O and Cu-O bonds belonging to the oxidized state.
